name: Kaysone Phomvihane Thought
summary: The official ideology of the Lao People's Revolutionary Party, a Lao adaptation of Marxism-Leninism and Ho Chi Minh Thought. It aims at socialism in an underdeveloped country without a full capitalist stage, led by a vanguard party, with state and cooperative ownership. After 1986 it combines party monopoly with markets, private enterprise and foreign investment under a 'socialist-oriented market economy'.
scope: The party line associated with Kaysone Phomvihane as Lao leader, 1955-1992, centred on his book Revolution in Laos (1980) and the 1986 New Economic Mechanism, as codified by the LPRP at its 10th Congress in 2016. It excludes critics' views and the practices of later leaders beyond what the 2016 codification states. Wikipedia and a 1980s primary text are the main evidence; the official documents are largely not available in English, so many answers are inferred.

keyFigures.name: Kaysone Phomvihane

sources.usedFor: Biography, Vietnam and Soviet ties, party leadership from 1955, commemoration.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Kaysone's account credits the party with building a public health service and national hygiene and preventive-medicine campaigns as socialist achievements, though it does not state a universal guarantee.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from a worker-peasant party's general pro-labour orientation, with Laos's low-wage development setting making it a weak commitment.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Even after the 1986 New Economic Mechanism the party uses markets only as a tool under state leadership, and Kaysone insists the state must not abandon its economic-directing duties.

public-ownership.rationale: The programme in Revolution in Laos puts socialist ownership in two forms, state and cooperative, in the commanding position of the national economy.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the party's egalitarian socialist aims, tempered by its later courting of private and foreign capital.

unions-good.rationale: The book treats trade unions as mass organisations that the party builds and uses to educate and mobilise workers, so they are valued, though as party-led bodies.

property-fundamental.rationale: Private property is tolerated and used under the NEM, but the doctrine subordinates it to socialist ownership and the people's democratic state.

regulate-corporations.rationale: A state that directs the economy and, under the NEM, welcomes private enterprise would regulate it tightly in the party's name.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not addressed directly; a socialist-oriented party credits social services as achievements and would not frame welfare as dependency.

worker-ownership.rationale: Cooperative ownership is one of the two socialist forms in the programme, but the emphasis is on state and cooperative rather than enterprise-level worker ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from a one-party security state that prioritises order and defence against subversion.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the conservative social-order stance of Marxist-Leninist ruling parties.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not discussed; the party treats national unity of all nationalities as a core value and would back restrictions that protect it.

strong-leader.rationale: The book stresses collective leadership and democratic centralism within the party rather than a leader bypassing institutions.

state-harmful.rationale: Marxist-Leninism as Kaysone applies it requires a strong people's democratic state exercising the dictatorship of the proletariat to build socialism.

limit-guns.rationale: Not discussed; a state that monopolises revolutionary violence in the party-led army would keep private arms tightly controlled.

empower-police-military.rationale: The armed forces are called the principal instrument of revolutionary violence, but funding questions are not discussed.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from conventional socialist-state social policy and Lao law.

decide-locally.rationale: Kaysone says that economic decentralisation does not mean local authorities have complete freedom; democratic centralism keeps decisions with the centre.

rehabilitation.rationale: The book stresses ideological re-education of people and small producers, which suggests a corrective rather than purely punitive approach; penal policy itself is not discussed.

traditional-family.rationale: Not discussed; the party backs equal rights for men and women but is socially conservative in practice, so adherents are split.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the party's conservative social line.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not discussed; Lao law restricts abortion and nothing in the doctrine pushes against that.

more-religion-public.rationale: The programme tolerates patriotic religious faiths in the united front but does not give religion a larger public role.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The book champions equality of all nationalities and support for upland peoples, which reads as backing corrective policy, though 'racial' injustice is not the framing.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not discussed; the party backs equal rights for women but has no stated theory of gender.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Kaysone grounds the revolution in Lao resistance history and a mass movement for education and culture, while the party calls for national-form culture.

gradual-change.rationale: The ideology is revolutionary, though it speaks of a long, staged transition to socialism; adherents lean against deference to existing institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not discussed; immigration is a marginal issue in doctrine.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Not discussed; Kaysone favours non-aligned cooperation toward a new international economic order but gives no stance on empowering the UN.

free-trade.rationale: The NEM liberalised trade and foreign investment, but the doctrine's anti-imperialism and state economic direction make it uncertain.

nation-first.rationale: Kaysone combines national independence with proletarian internationalism and Indochinese solidarity, so the statement splits his position.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The book condemns imperialist intervention and upholds respect for each country's sovereignty.

open-borders.rationale: Borders are eventually obsolete in Marxist theory, but nothing in this ideology proposes them; Laos stresses sovereignty and border demarcation.

limit-growth.rationale: Not discussed; a poor country building socialism prioritises production growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not discussed; the doctrine pre-dates climate politics.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The programme treats science, technology and modern production as keys to development, but does not claim they solve most problems.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Nuclear power is not addressed in Kaysone's writings or the Lao party line; Laos's hydropower focus and the party's neutral stance on energy technology leave this unplaceable.

revolution-justified.rationale: Revolution in Laos describes the national democratic revolution and its direct transition to socialism, relying on revolutionary violence.

experts-over-public.rationale: Authority rests with the vanguard party and the masses, not technocrats; it is not discussed directly.

central-planning.rationale: The 1979-86 planned economy stagnated and the party moved to the NEM, so adherents now favour state leadership with market mechanisms rather than pure planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: The NEM and the 'socialist-oriented market economy' accept markets alongside state and collective enterprises under state direction.

land-value-tax.rationale: Neither the book nor the NEM material mentions a land-value tax, and since land is state-controlled in a socialist system the single-tax idea has no obvious pull.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from socialist egalitarianism.

basic-income.rationale: Not discussed; the doctrine favours work and production over unconditional transfers.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from state-led development and an independent national economy.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The party-led state steers development, with state economic bodies keeping their directing role even under reform.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The programme aims to bring small producers, artisans and farmers into cooperatives and collective production.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: A long-term communist aim, but the Lao party stresses a long transitional period and uses markets today.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not discussed; a state-led economy would keep a state bank.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Mass organisations including unions are party-led, which resembles state-recognised bodies, but the idea is not framed corporatively.

one-party-rule.rationale: The book insists that victory requires leadership by the vanguard Marxist-Leninist party, and the Lao constitution enshrines the party's leading role.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The 1975 Congress of People's Representatives dismantled the monarchy and Kaysone describes the feudal-monarchical system as overthrown.

democracy-best.rationale: The ideology is a 'people's democratic state' under party leadership and democratic centralism rather than competitive multiparty democracy.

direct-votes.rationale: Not discussed; the system works through congresses and representatives under party guidance.

workers-councils.rationale: Power rests on the people's democratic state led by the party, with a worker-peasant alliance, not on independent councils.

right-to-secede.rationale: Not discussed directly; the book stresses unity of all nationalities within one Lao state.

natural-rulers.rationale: Leadership is justified by vanguard role and correct theory, not natural fitness to rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: Kaysone calls the armed forces the principal instrument of revolutionary violence and relies on that violence.

war-builds-character.rationale: The book presents war as forced upon Laos by imperialists rather than as a virtue.

separate-church-state.rationale: The constitution lists freedom of religion, and the programme includes religious faiths in the front; the state is secular but supervises religion.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist state bases law on party-state programme and socialist legality, not scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: State coercive institutions are core to the people's democratic state; private provision is incompatible.

military-superiority.rationale: Not discussed; Laos relied on Vietnamese and Soviet alliance rather than seeking superiority.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The book celebrates the unity of all nationalities in Laos and equality among them.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The book treats national and democratic questions as tied to class struggle and calls for detailed class analysis, a Marxist-Leninist core.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Socialist ownership and the aim of equality of classes point toward outcome equality, though the Lao party accepts inequality under the NEM.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not discussed; land is held by the state and nationalities are integrated into one state.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the strong anti-colonial and anti-imperialist stance and the call for a new international economic order.

civilizational-union.rationale: The ideology looks to ideological solidarity (Indochina, socialist bloc) rather than civilisational unity.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Socialist ethics stress collective interest and cooperation against exploitation.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Not discussed directly; collectivist doctrine stresses duty to the people and party.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The sources treat nature as a resource for development and say nothing of intrinsic value, so adherents have no settled position either way.

limit-population.rationale: Not discussed; the doctrine locates poverty in social relations, not population.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The programme aims at industrialisation and modern production as a basis of socialism.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on science, technology and developing productive forces.

human-enhancement.rationale: Body and mind enhancement is outside anything in Kaysone's thought; the party's silence on bioethics means no position can be inferred.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Not discussed; leadership is by the party.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from a security-minded single-party state.

restore-past-order.rationale: The party's founding aim was to overthrow the feudal-monarchical order and prevent its restoration.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The NEM and 'new thinking' were pragmatic, yet the party insists on applying Marxism-Leninism creatively, so adherents are split.

direct-action.rationale: The ideology favours party-led organised struggle and uses elections and coalition politics tactically, not spontaneous direct action.

means-match-ends.rationale: The doctrine justifies coercive transitional means (dictatorship of the proletariat) for a classless end.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The programme aims at modern socialist production and development.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: A far-future Marxist aim, but not a practical commitment in Laos.

distribute-by-need.rationale: A communist ideal beyond the socialist stage; the party stresses distribution by labour in the present.

production-for-use.rationale: Socialist production aims at meeting people's needs, as against capitalist profit, in Marxist-Leninist doctrine.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The book treats capitalist and feudal forms as exploitative, though the NEM allows private profit in practice.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The book names the tasks of the dictatorship of the proletariat, including building socialism while bypassing capitalism.

collective-farming.rationale: The programme calls for farmers to form agricultural cooperatives and adopt collective production, though the party retreated from forced collectivisation.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Kaysone's analysis casts imperialism as aggressive and links the world crisis to it, in the standard Leninist way.

taxation-theft.rationale: The state taxes to finance development; the idea of taxes as theft is alien to socialist doctrine.

harm-principle.rationale: Not discussed; the party-state restricts conduct for socialist and national goals too.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Collective and class rights, such as nationalities' equality, are emphasised.

conscription.rationale: Not discussed; a people's army built from the masses is the model.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Not discussed; the ideology privileges participation within the party-led system.

state-as-business.rationale: The ideology views the state as a socialist instrument of the working people, not a firm serving customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on material emancipation of peasants and workers through socialist transformation.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not discussed; the party sees itself as holding power through the state.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The doctrine of equal nationalities rejects racial ranking.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation runs through party-led congresses and mass organisations, not families and guilds.

total-state.rationale: The party-state is expansive, but the NEM shows tolerance for a private and foreign economic sector.

national-rebirth.rationale: Not discussed; the ideology speaks of socialist construction, not decadence and rebirth.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The book condemns great-power chauvinism and stresses sovereignty and equality among Indochina's states.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: A feudal pattern that the revolution aimed to abolish.

bound-labor.rationale: The book describes liberated areas doing away with feudal and prefeudal forms of exploitation.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Marxist class-based views of ideology would agree in part, but this is not discussed in the sources.

universal-morality.rationale: Marxism treats morality as class-conditioned; Lao sources do not address it.

single-common-good.rationale: Not discussed; the ideology sees interests as class-differentiated, though the front unites patriotic classes.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The Lao party's writings do not take up the Israel question; the sources give no basis for a position, so this stays at neutral.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora return rights are never discussed in Kaysone's thought, and nothing in the principles points clearly either way.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not discussed; Lao is the working language already.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from stress on collective management by working people.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education is built as a public service by the socialist state.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal stance on deficits is not in the sources; the party's state-led economy could justify stimulus while its stability concerns could cut the other way.

economic-freedom.rationale: The ideology holds that political power must lead the economy; economic liberalisation is conducted under party monopoly.

rule-by-example.rationale: Party cadres are asked for exemplary conduct, but the system relies on law and organisation too.

national-self-determination.rationale: The book frames the revolution as a struggle for national independence against French and American domination.

force-without-un.rationale: Not discussed; the doctrine stresses sovereignty and non-interference.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Marxism-Leninism claims scientific grounding, though the party tolerates patriotic believers.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The sources do not discuss welfare eligibility by citizenship, and socialist universalism pulls against nation-based limits, so it is left neutral.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not discussed; labour is treated as a duty and basis of distribution under socialism.

class-collaboration.rationale: The party opposes class conciliation in principle, though it allies with the national bourgeoisie that accepts socialist transformation.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not discussed; the party values national culture and history.

dominated-front.rationale: Kaysone promotes cooperation with non-aligned countries for a new international economic order against imperialist domination.

workers-nation.rationale: Proletarian internationalism is the standard; the book says that the Laotian revolution is part of the Indochina and world revolution.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The programme lists equal rights of men and women among its democratic rights.

ban-interest.rationale: Not discussed; state banking and credit exist alongside markets.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The book affirms equality of all nationalities and unity among them.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marxist-Leninist theory, which the Lao party follows, treats the state as the instrument of a ruling class; hence the people's state is the workers' and peasants' tool.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Domestic fossil-fuel production is not discussed in the sources; the party's development priority suggests openness but nothing is stated.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Not discussed; the party celebrates the cultural equality of Laos's nationalities.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy-style claim outside Marxist-Leninist analysis.

proportional-representation.rationale: Not discussed; representation is organised under party direction.

national-mission.rationale: The Lao party stresses its own national path and not exporting its system.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Not discussed directly; the party's equal-rights line implies inequality as a problem.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The party presents itself as the people's vanguard; this critique is not endorsed.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics is alien to the socialist programme and its emphasis on social causes.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not discussed; the party-state would resist external accountability.

night-watchman-state.rationale: A socialist state directs the economy and society.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Equality of all nationalities is a founding principle.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Equality of nationalities and of men and women is declared a democratic right.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The Lao party builds socialism in Laos itself, bypassing capitalism, with fraternal support from Vietnam and the USSR but not awaiting others' revolutions.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Settler colonialism as a category is not discussed; Kaysone's anti-colonial writing concerns French and American domination of Laos, not settler states.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Not discussed; a unitary state with equality among nationalities points to uniform law.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The sources only record religious faiths as part of the patriotic front; whether conversion should be legally restricted is not addressed.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not discussed; not an issue in Lao socialism.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Inferred from a secular socialist state controlling education.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The book treats imperialist hostility as a reason to strengthen the people's state and its armed forces while building socialism.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The party claims legitimacy from the people through a people's democratic state, though not through competitive elections.

trade-surplus.rationale: Kaysone's thought does not discuss trade balances; the NEM opened trade and foreign investment without stating an export-surplus aim.

population-transfer.rationale: Not discussed; contradicts the proclaimed unity of nationalities.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Revolutionary violence and state coercion are accepted; this absolutist principle is rejected.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The doctrine stresses cooperation and class solidarity; competition between peoples is alien to it.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Inferred from a one-party state that bars parties.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Not discussed; the language of freedom from domination fits the anti-colonial struggle.

separated-powers.rationale: Democratic centralism and party leadership give a unified power structure, not checks.

vanguard-party.rationale: The book states victory requires a vanguard party of the working class applying Marxism-Leninism creatively.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The programme addresses peasants and workers as its base and aims to fix the needs of poor peasants.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Council-housing sales are a British issue and the Lao sources say nothing on it; socialist ownership principles would lean against it but weakly.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Not discussed; unions are party-led, and strikes are not a theme.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Marxist analysis ties poverty to social and colonial relations, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The book celebrates growing unity of all nationalities in Laos.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not discussed; offices are filled by party selection and election.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Not discussed; the state is prepared to use extraordinary measures to defend the revolution.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Not discussed; the state-directed economy used price setting, though the NEM liberalised many prices.

party-controls-media.rationale: Not discussed in sources; Lao media are party-state controlled in practice.

party-commands-army.rationale: The book describes a worker-peasant army under the leadership of the Party.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation periods are outside the sources, and Laos's small immigration makes the issue marginal to the doctrine.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from egalitarian socialist ethics for cadres.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The book cites building democratic centralism within the party and fighting indiscipline.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Not discussed; the ideology stresses sovereignty, though it favours Indochinese cooperation.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The party, not an individual head of state, commands.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not discussed; irrelevant to Lao Buddhism and socialism.

clerical-rule.rationale: Political authority belongs to the party, not religious scholars.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: A Leninist idea, but Kaysone's sources address national liberation wars rather than great-power wars.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Not discussed; party-led culture is meant to serve socialist education.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Not discussed; Kaysone led the party from 1955 to 1991 without a term limit.

recall-officials.rationale: The sources mention democratic centralism within the party but not voter recall of officials, so no position can be read from them.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Kaysone prized the special Laos-Vietnam solidarity and ties with the USSR.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Housing tenure is not discussed in Kaysone's writings; the idea of banning rent has no source in the Lao programme.

people-in-arms.rationale: The party built a people's army from armed detachments, but later set up a regular army.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The party builds its base among peasants but does not claim rural life is morally better, and it aims at industrialisation, so this is left neutral.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Not discussed; Laos itself was unified, and the party celebrated Indochinese revolutionary unity.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not discussed; the party values the intelligentsia as allies.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Inferred from the stress on equality of Laos's nationalities.

death-penalty.rationale: Not discussed; Lao law retains capital punishment.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: School sex education is not discussed; a socialist state expanding education and health services would plausibly support it, though the sources do not say so.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not discussed; party cultural policy is moralistic.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship rules are not covered by the sources; unity of all nationalities in Laos does not resolve descent versus birthplace.

minority-language-support.rationale: The book stresses equality and cultural development of all nationalities, including mountain peoples.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not discussed; a uniform legal order is preferred.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Not discussed; the party stresses collective discipline.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the call for a new international economic order.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The party's line is that the national democratic revolution must pass directly to socialist transformation of production relations.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The 1975 Congress of People's Representatives proclaimed the republic and drew up a programme.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The NEM combined economic liberalisation with continued party monopoly.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Kaysone calls for a new international economic order, which fits aid duties, but aid itself is not discussed.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: A nuclear arsenal for Laos is never contemplated in the sources; Laos relied on Vietnamese and Soviet alliance, which weakly suggests a no.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The sources discuss congresses and representatives, not how the head of state should be chosen, so there is no clear position.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The state directs the economy and monetary policy is not independent.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Not discussed; the Laos-Vietnam border settlement shows readiness to compromise.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Private property is allowed only insofar as it serves socialist construction; the people's democratic state utilises it.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Kaysone honoured the USSR as the leading socialist state and received its orders.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk policy is absent from Kaysone's writings, so adherents have no documented stance on acting before scientific certainty.

collective-defense.rationale: The book stresses mutual assistance among Indochinese peoples and the socialist community.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Not discussed; the anti-imperialist logic points that way.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Not discussed; religion is placed under party-state supervision in practice.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The state is a party-led state.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Not discussed; unity of the state and nationalities is a core aim.

region-keeps-system.rationale: A region joining a larger state with its own system is not discussed; the Lao party stresses unity of its own nationalities in one state.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Monarchy was abolished and religion is not used for state sanctity.

flat-income-tax.rationale: A socialist state favours progressive taxation.

character-from-environment.rationale: Marxist materialism holds that social conditions form people, and the book stresses re-education.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The ideology stresses socialist legality and collective party discipline, even though the party sits above the legal order.

space-expansion.rationale: Space expansion is outside the thought's concerns; the party focuses on national construction and development.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Not discussed; the system is a single-party state.

leader-cult.rationale: Kaysone has a museum, banknote portrait and thought named after him.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody presumptions are not covered; the programme's equal rights of men and women does not settle post-separation parenting.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The Lao party sees classes persisting in transition but does not accept the Maoist claim that party leaders may restore capitalism.

land-redistribution.rationale: Kaysone says that the slogan 'Land to the Tillers' was not the slogan that reflected Lao peasants' needs; the priority was joint struggle and production.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee return is not in the sources; many Lao fled after 1975, but the party's stated position on their return is not documented here.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The book stresses sovereignty and opposes great-power chauvinism.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Contrary to the freedom-of-religion line in the constitution.

women-must-cover.rationale: Equal rights for women are programme policy.

common-currency.rationale: Shared currencies are not discussed; Kaysone wrote of Indochinese cooperation but without any monetary union.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The sources stress unity of nationalities within Laos and Indochinese solidarity, not political union of peoples by language family.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Not discussed; the party affirms equality of nationalities within one state.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The statement is about minorities elsewhere; Kaysone's sources do not address diaspora minorities and strategy.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Marxism-Leninism as the base of the thought puts production relations at the core of historical change.

ban-cartels.rationale: Antitrust policy is not discussed; the state-directed economy has few private cartels, and the sources give no stance.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailouts of firms and banks are not covered in the sources; state-owned enterprises dominating the economy make the question marginal.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Not discussed; in a people's democratic state courts are not counter-majoritarian.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Not discussed; equal rights of men and women are programme policy.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The party solicits foreign aid, cooperation with socialist states and later foreign investment, not an autarkic bloc.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Binding labour and environmental clauses in trade agreements are not discussed; the NEM focuses on trade openness without such terms.

moral-incentives.rationale: Labour campaigns and re-education are mentioned, but material incentives returned under the NEM.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The book credits mass base and party organisation, not a foco, though armed forces grew from support bases.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The revolution dismantled the monarchy and feudal order.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The book itself centres Lao national history and resistance.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The ideology is anti-colonial and opposes imperial domination.

patriotic-education.rationale: The party stresses ideological and political education and national history.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not discussed; equality of nationalities is stressed.

public-money-creation.rationale: Not discussed; money creation is a state function.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Marxism-Leninism treats capitalism as in general crisis, though the party now uses capitalist methods.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Not discussed; Laos was a colonised state.

delink-world-market.rationale: The NEM opened Laos to foreign investment and trade.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The labour-aristocracy thesis is a Leninist idea, but Kaysone's writings on imperialism do not take it up, so no position is documented.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Equality of nationalities and sexes is programme policy.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Entrenched judicial rights limits are not in the sources; the party-led people's democratic state does not frame rights as limits on majorities.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the anti-colonial stance.

elective-rulers.rationale: Not discussed; the people's democratic state rests on elected congresses.

minority-veto.rationale: Democratic centralism binds the minority to the majority decision.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The sources do not address resisting rulers who break constitutional law; the party's own revolution rejected a monarchy rather than a lawless ruler.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Not discussed; the party leads over the assembly.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal sentience is not discussed in Kaysone's thought; the statement is mild enough that adherents would not oppose it, but nothing is stated.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Humane animal use is not covered in the sources; no position follows from the party's agricultural focus except general acceptance.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The ideology rejects paternalism of elites in favour of class power.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Party members are expected to be active cadres.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Frankfurt-school style critique of mass culture is absent; Kaysone's thought addresses imperialist propaganda, not mass culture generally.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Hegemony through consent is a Gramscian idea the Lao sources do not use, so adherents are neither clearly for nor against.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Kaysone's anti-imperialism holds that colonial and imperial powers exploit poor countries.

native-born-offices.rationale: Reserving offices for native-born citizens is not discussed; the programme's equality of nationalities within Laos does not decide the question.

party-own-road.rationale: The book says the vanguard party must apply Marxism-Leninism creatively to the country's conditions, though within the Indochinese and socialist-bloc community.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Kaysone stresses independence yet Laos depended on Vietnamese and Soviet aid.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Border demarcation with Vietnam was settled by agreement.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The sources treat all nationalities as equal in one state and say nothing of leadership by pre-colonial descendants, so a mild no is inferred.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Not discussed; the socialist camp's anti-fascist heritage is cited in the book's WWII narrative.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The party reveres the Soviet victory over fascism and rejects equating communism with fascism.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: American Civil War causes are outside the sources; Marxist historiography generally reads that war as about slavery, which implies a mild no.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monument policy is not discussed; the party's own use of memorials to its leaders gives no basis for a position on contested ones.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Men's disadvantage is not a theme in Kaysone's thought, whose gender content is limited to equal rights of men and women.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Domestic-violence policy is not covered in the sources; the programme's equal rights line gives no stance on symmetry.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The doctrine insists on a distinct path suited to Laos, rather than liberal democracy.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Not discussed; the army is subordinate to the party.

paid-care-work.rationale: Wages for domestic work are not discussed; Marxist-Leninist socialisation of care is plausible but not stated in the Lao sources.

filial-duty.rationale: Family duties are not addressed; Lao social norms and the party's conservative social line weakly support filial respect.

office-by-exam.rationale: Not discussed; party cadres are selected by political criteria.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Not discussed; the NEM courted foreign investment.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Divorce law is not discussed; equal rights between spouses implies mild support but no source states it.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Binding mandate and recall of delegates, a council-communist idea, is not in Kaysone's writings; democratic centralism binds leaders to the party instead.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: A socialist state favours state-provided social insurance.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliamentary budget approval is not discussed; under party leadership the assembly's budget role is not a stated principle.

single-official-language.rationale: Language policy is not addressed beyond equality of nationalities, which pulls against a single sole language while Lao is the common one.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Disparate-impact doctrine is a US legal concept the sources do not touch; equality of nationalities gives no clear answer.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Not discussed; socialist ethics criticise it.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The book backs national liberation struggles in proletarian internationalism terms; it does not discuss arming them.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Not discussed; Vietnamese forces served in Laos, but this is not a stated doctrine.

corporate-influence.rationale: Marxist-Leninist analysis sees capital as dominating politics in capitalist states.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the party-state's control of civil society.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Population policy is not discussed; Laos has not been a notable pronatalist state in the sources, so no position can be read.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local limits on property purchases are not mentioned in the sources, and state land ownership makes the question marginal.

job-guarantee.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from socialist state commitment to work.

democratic-peace.rationale: Leninist theory sees capitalist democracies as imperialist.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: A general duty to obey the law is not discussed; the stress on socialist legality and party discipline weakly counts against a no-duty view.

non-intervention.rationale: The book stresses respect for each country's sovereignty and equality.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure by industry versus craft is not discussed; unions are described only as party-led mass organisations.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Alien to the doctrine's unity of nationalities.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The sources never question legal marriage; equal rights of men and women are stated within the existing family-law framework.

public-access-to-information.rationale: A right of access to government information is not in the sources; a one-party state with democratic centralism does not stress it.

local-production.rationale: Local production for local consumption is not discussed; the NEM and trade liberalisation point toward market integration instead.

informal-organisation.rationale: The party insists on disciplined, formal party organisation.

religious-nation.rationale: The nation is a union of nationalities and faiths in the patriotic front.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Not discussed; the book condemns great-power chauvinism.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Not discussed; centralism keeps revenue with the national state.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Marxist-Leninist doctrine keeps personal property distinct from means of production.

defeat-communism.rationale: The party's whole project is communist construction.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Mixed public, private and independent service delivery is not addressed, though the NEM allows private enterprise beside state firms.

religion-illusion.rationale: Marxist doctrine says so, but Kaysone's practice sought alliance with religious believers.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Marxism holds that capitalism builds the productive base, and the NEM uses state capitalism for that purpose.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not discussed explicitly; Marxist-Leninist theory links the two.

socialized-care.rationale: Public provision of childcare and housework is a classic socialist aim, but the sources on Laos do not mention it.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purism is not discussed in the Lao sources and plays no role in the party's programme.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with internal nations are not covered; the Lao state treats nationalities as equal citizens, not treaty partners.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The programme calls for cooperatives within a centrally led socialist state, not small self-governing communities.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The thought is explicitly Marxist-Leninist, aiming at socialism by bypassing capitalism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Historic ties to land are invoked in Kaysone's account of Lao resistance to Siamese and Burmese domination, but no claim principle is stated.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Same-sex relations are not discussed in the sources, and Laos has not criminalised them, so a mild no is the inference.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The party monopoly and the dictatorship of the proletariat rule out an organised opposition.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Contrary to a secular programme and the freedom-of-religion line.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The book condemns French colonial exploitation as the enemy.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: An Islamic doctrine on armed resistance has no place in a secular Marxist-Leninist ideology, though the book itself supports resistance to invaders.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Contrary to a secular, Marxist-Leninist state.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The book speaks of mass participation in the people's democratic state, but within party leadership.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Intersectional analysis is not used in Kaysone's thought, which privileges class analysis, so no position is documented.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Gender identity law is not discussed; the party's conservative social line suggests a mild no.

assisted-dying.rationale: Assisted dying is not discussed in any Lao party source, and Buddhism-influenced Lao society gives no clear signal.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marxist theory holds so, though Lao sources do not use the concept.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Contrary to the equality of faiths and nationalities.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Authority comes from the people and the party.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Employment contract limits are not discussed; pro-worker leanings would support them but Kaysone's writings do not mention it.

social-market-economy.rationale: The NEM combines markets with state leadership and socialist orientation, a related but different model.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The book treats armed forces as essential to defending the revolution.

rich-first.rationale: The NEM encouraged private enterprise, but the sources do not state this principle.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Laos aligned with Vietnam and the USSR in the socialist camp.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Contrary to the abolition of monarchy.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutual credit banks are not discussed; the NEM relies on state and commercial banking instead.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Austerity conditions of international lenders are not covered by the sources, and the NEM involved opening to such lenders.

property-franchise.rationale: The people's democratic state gives rights to workers and peasants, not property owners.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminist claims are not in the Lao sources, which address women's equality only as a democratic right.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept, not used in Lao sources.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The ML critique of bourgeois democracy matches the argument.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Not discussed; socialist legality is a stated aim.

racial-franchise.rationale: Contrary to the equality of nationalities.

online-participation.rationale: Online deliberation is outside the thought, which predates it; the party's top-down organisation gives no signal.

open-government-data.rationale: Not discussed; the party-state is secretive.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Contrary to the national unity line.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Random assemblies are not discussed; participation runs through party-led congresses and mass organisations.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Reinterpreting religious doctrine is not Kaysone's concern; he treats religion as a matter of patriotic alliance, not doctrine.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The doctrine opposes concentrated private capital as exploitative.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Military service by gay people is not discussed in Kaysone's thought and nothing points clearly either way.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Marxist doctrine is atheist, but Kaysone's united front welcomed religious believers and the constitution protects religion.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: A coercive state apparatus is needed during socialist construction.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Coalitions were a tactic, not a principle.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The socialist state is expected to provide for social needs.

term-limits.rationale: Term limits are not addressed; Kaysone led the party for 36 years and the sources say nothing on limits.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid delegation of votes is not discussed; the system runs on party-led representative congresses, so a mild no is inferred.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Extinction risk is not a theme of the thought; Kaysone's writings centre on national development and anti-imperialism.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: The sources do not address religious offices; the party defers to religious bodies outside politics, so no position is read.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Equal rights of men and women are programme policy.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Voting by foreign residents is not discussed; a sovereignty-focused one-party state would weakly oppose it.

rent-control.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from state intervention in the economy.

abolish-ip.rationale: Intellectual property is not discussed; the sources give no basis, though Marxist views on private ownership of knowledge are mixed.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The book describes youth organisations as party-led mass organisations.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Nuclear basing is not discussed, but an anti-imperialist small state would resist foreign nuclear weapons on its territory.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Not discussed; the anti-imperialist line opposes foreign bases of rivals.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Formal recognition of past genocides is not discussed in the Lao sources, and nothing indicates a stance.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Marxism-Leninism treats profit from ownership as exploitation and favours pay for labour, though the post-1986 market line tolerates private returns.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Kaysone's account presents the revolution as an armed struggle and defence of the nation, so a pacifist ban on lethal force is foreign to it.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred from the party's appeal to the Lao people's long tradition of resistance to foreign rule; the sources do not discuss ancient continuity directly.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred from orthodox Marxism-Leninism, which treats sex as biological and addresses only women's social roles; the sources do not discuss this.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from the party's mass-organisation model, in which women are one unified constituency under the party line; not discussed directly.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from the party's commemoration of revolutionary heroes and fallen fighters, which is public but secular rather than sacred.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Dialectical and historical materialism explain politics as class struggle, not a spiritual contest between good and evil.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred from a state-centred, territorial nationalism; the party does not frame the Lao homeland as a cultural centre for a diaspora.

culture-before-state.rationale: Kaysone's account makes seizing and holding state power through the party first, with culture transformed afterwards under that power.

god-not-male.rationale: The party is atheist in outlook but guarantees religious freedom and is indifferent to how God is described.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from materialist views that subordinate religion to party policy and do not use women's humanity as a test of scripture.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Kaysone stresses equality among Laos's many nationalities and the 1986 line welcomes foreign and state enterprise, not majority-run commerce.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred from the party's multi-ethnic framework of equal nationalities; merging regions by people is not discussed.

independent-unions.rationale: Kaysone's account places mass organisations including unions under party leadership, so independence from the ruling party is rejected.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The party presents itself as the vanguard of the worker-peasant alliance, with power held by the working people.

local-essentials-public.rationale: State and cooperative ownership of key services fits the programme, though post-1986 markets allow private provision; inferred.

second-chamber.rationale: Laos has a unicameral National Assembly under party leadership; a second chamber is not part of the line.

municipal-property.rationale: The programme calls for state and cooperative ownership, not community ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Democratic centralism places decisions with the party and the central organs, not local assemblies.

family-wage.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from a conventional socialist pro-worker stance.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Never addressed; no basis in the sources for a side.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Never addressed; no basis in the sources for a side.

anonymous-payments.rationale: A one-party state seeking control of the economy would oppose untraceable payments; inferred.

online-anonymity.rationale: Party monopoly on politics implies opposition to anonymity; inferred.

person-over-state.rationale: Marxism-Leninism subordinates the individual to the collective and party; inferred.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Official Marxist-Leninist ideology is materialist; inferred.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: A unitary one-party state keeps local powers subject to central control; inferred.

gm-crops.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the push for agricultural modernisation under the New Economic Mechanism.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed; no basis in the sources for a side.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Marxism-Leninism organises by class and nation, not by race; inferred.

racial-pride.rationale: Not addressed; Lao national pride is emphasised but racial pride is not.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The revolution was won by armed struggle, but the party line does not address this as a general rule; split.

missingStatements.text: A country can move to socialism directly from a pre-capitalist society without passing through a capitalist stage of development.
missingStatements.rationale: Kaysone's book describes the direct transition to socialism bypassing capitalism as the party's central strategic line.
missingStatements.declined: Stage-skipping thesis is specific to Marxist-Leninist strategy and tracked loosely by material-conditions-drive-history; not worth a statement.

missingStatements.text: A communist party should keep a special relationship of close alliance with the parties of neighbouring socialist countries.
missingStatements.rationale: The book describes the Laos revolution as an integral part of the Indochina revolution and stresses solidarity with Vietnam and Kampuchea.
missingStatements.declined: Bloc-specific alliance between ruling parties; party-own-road already covers the party-independence question.

notes: Official English-language texts of the 2016 codification were not found; many positions beyond economics, party and foreign policy are inferred from Marxist-Leninist orthodoxy and Lao party practice and marked low confidence. The 1980 book predates the NEM, so market-related answers combine it with the Wikipedia NEM summary.
